# Tasks

This is the team's shared task board. The PM creates entries; every agent updates the
status flag for the tasks it touches. This file is the single source of truth for work
state — the `/shell-team:run` loop advances the flag at each phase gate.

## Status flags

`READY_FOR_ARCH` → `READY_FOR_ENG` → `READY_FOR_QA` → `READY_FOR_REVIEW` → `READY_FOR_MERGE`
(or `BLOCKED` / `REWORK` at any stage)

### Local test result — T-1104 (engineer, rework round 2)

**Scope: implement the v2 (`c24efed`) per-section semantics the class-B re-freeze froze, and fix the codex round-1 implementation review's 1 Blocker's script-side consequence plus its 4 Majors and 3 Minors.** The Blocker itself was a frozen-region contradiction (AC4/AC21/Non-goals) already closed by `pm-spec`'s v1→v2 re-freeze; this round's job is the implementation the re-freeze requires plus the four independently-reproduced Majors and three Minors.

**Per-section completeness (DP-4/AC4 v2).** `bin/check-review-input.sh` now arms a verdict-heading section the moment IT carries any of the four fields; once armed it must carry at least one pass id all four of whose field lines resolve to that SAME section — a pass id credited from its earliest field line alone (v1's defect, and the review's own Major 4) is no longer credited to anything unless all four of its lines agree. A section carrying none of the four fields is conformant regardless of the rest of the record. Field/vocabulary/shape rules (`field-missing`/`field-duplicate`/`pass-id-charset`/vocabularies/`raw-capture-stem-mismatch`) run first, record-wide, so `field-missing` and `section-incomplete` stay disjoint exactly as the Goal's refusal-precedence clause requires.

**The 4 Majors, each reproduced live before the fix and again after (red → green):**
1. **Dangling-symlink fail-open** at both `--task`-only auto-resolution points (the reviews dir, the per-task record path): `[ ! -e "$P" ]` treated a broken symlink as "does not exist" and took the forward-only leniency. Fixed by adding `[ ! -L "$P" ]` to the same conjunct, so a broken occupant now falls through to the existing fail-closed `-d`/`-f`+`-r` tests (`reviews-dir-unresolvable` / `record-unreadable`).
2. **Tab-delimited internal transport bypass**: a literal tab inside a captured id or value could shift the internal TSV work file's column boundaries and truncate a value to a shorter, conformant-looking prefix before the vocabulary check ran. Fixed by rejecting any captured id or value containing a literal tab outright, at capture time, with `field-grammar` — before it ever reaches the (unchanged) tab-delimited work file.
3. **`raw-capture-collision` no-echo violation**: the refusal interpolated the actual colliding stem value into stderr, contradicting the script's own documented no-echo discipline (and the existing "no-echo case 2" test in `tests/check-review-input/run.sh` embedded its marker in the wrong field — `executor-invocation` rather than `raw-capture` — so it never actually exercised this bug). Fixed by naming only the refusal token and the two colliding pass ids; the pre-existing test's fixture corrected to embed its marker in `raw-capture` (the field the refusal actually reads), plus a fresh fixture.
4. **Section-ownership not section-scoped** — the same class as the Blocker's own repair, one rule per the re-freeze's own framing: a pass id is now credited to a section only when ALL FOUR of its field lines resolve to that section (computed via a new 5th "owner" column stamped onto every extracted field line, using the heading-line extraction moved earlier in the script so it runs before field extraction).

**Minors:** `export LC_ALL=C` added once, near the top (after `set -euo pipefail`), closing the whole bracket-class/collation hazard class in one line rather than scoping it per call site. The `2>/dev/null || true` field-scan and heading-scan pipelines now distinguish a real `grep` failure (exit > 1) from a clean no-match (exit 1) via `die "record-unreadable: ..."`; the `raw-capture` stem-duplicate detection pipeline (`cut`/`sort`/`uniq -d`) was similarly de-masked. The `agents/codex-reviewer.md:206`/`:212` textual-inconsistency Minor was left as the reviewer's own recommendation states (non-blocking, at the coordinating session's discretion) — not touched this round.

### Rework round 2 — T-1103 (engineer, answering the codex round-1 implementation review's 2 Blockers, 2 Majors, 2 Minors)

**Blocker 1 (integer overflow in the anchor equality) — closed.** `bin/check-oversight.sh`'s `specify-seam` anchor regex is narrowed from `^v[0-9]+$` to `^v(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,14})$` (at most 15 digits, no leading zero), bounding the digit run BEFORE any `$((10#$N))` arithmetic runs on it, rather than attempting arithmetic on unbounded input. Refuses with the existing `approval-anchor-malformed` token. Fixtures added: `v18446744073709551617` (the exact overflow value from the review's reproduction), a 20-digit value (`v99999999999999999999`), and a leading-zero form (`v01`) — all three refuse `approval-anchor-malformed`.

**Blocker 2 (field forgery through `record=`'s free-form value) — closed.** The three independent greedy-`sed -E` field extractions are replaced with a single left-to-right pass over the raw record string, using bash parameter-expansion pattern matching to consume exactly one ` — `-delimited `key=value` prefix per field before advancing, so `record=` — the only genuinely free-form field — receives whatever text remains, decoy included, with no way to influence where an earlier field is read from. **Adversarial finding during self-verification, disclosed rather than smuggled**: the review's own literal reproduction string does not reproduce on this sandbox (macOS BSD `sed`) — independently re-checked with BSD `sed`, Python `re` and Perl, all three resolve the review's exact decoy to the CORRECT value (`v1`), not the claimed `v999`, because that specific decoy has only one `date=`/`record=` occurrence in the line and the regex has no ambiguous split available. A genuinely ambiguous decoy — duplicating **both** `date=` and `record=` (not just `approves=`) after the real fields — does shift `approves_raw` under the pre-fix greedy-`sed` shape, confirmed with all three engines; in that specific arrangement the OLD code's `producer_raw` extraction also happens to corrupt into a `— `-laden string that fails `HANDLE_RE`, so the old code still refuses (wrongly, rejecting a fully conformant record) rather than silently accepting a forged version — a real defect (a legitimate record wrongly refused), just not the exact "silent security bypass" shape the review described for this string. The fix closes both shapes categorically, by construction, regardless of decoy complexity. Fixtures added (using the genuinely-ambiguous decoy shape): a conformant record with the decoy tail (must still pass, and does); a genuinely malformed record — `approves=` missing from its own slot — with a decoy `approves=` appended (must still refuse, and does, `approval-malformed`).

**Major 1 (absent arm never reads the shipped default) — closed.** The absent arm now resolves `templates/oversight-default.conf` from the checker's own installed directory (`TEMPLATES_ROOT`, one level above `SCRIPT_DIR`, computed the same way `bin/resolve-executor.sh:295`–`:296` computes its own) and routes it through the same `parse_config()` sibling a host declaration goes through — member for member with `resolve-executor.sh`'s absent arm, never a hardcoded literal. A missing or unreadable shipped default now refuses `declaration-unreadable` (exit 2), matching this task's own Input-space item and the script's pre-existing header documentation of that exact case. Fixtures added: a scratch `bin/`+`templates/` pair proving the present case resolves and prints the declared profile, and a `bin/`-only pair (no `templates/`) proving the missing case refuses exit 2. **Fallout discovered and fixed**: four pre-existing `tests/close-out/run.sh` fixtures that build a scratch `bin/` copy (`STUB_ROOT`, `RF_ROOT`, `HS_ROOT`, `STUB_SL_ROOT`) each had a positive-control case that only passed because the pre-fix absent arm never touched the filesystem; each is now widened with `cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/templates" "<root>/templates"` (the same shape `tests/check-adapter/run.sh:300` already uses), mirroring the real installed layout — reproduced live, fixed, and the full 120-assertion suite re-verified green.

**Major 2 (no-echo invariant violated) — closed.** The `approval-malformed` refusal for a grammar-mismatching record no longer interpolates the raw matched line; it now names the record's absolute board line number (`grep -n` against the already-extracted entry, offset by the entry's own start line) instead, matching the discipline every other refusal in the file already follows. Fixture added: a grammar-mismatching record carrying real-looking handle bytes (`reviewer-01`/`author-02`), asserted absent from stderr — the AC12-style no-echo assertion extended to the malformed class the review found untested.

**Minor 1 (`git log` failure swallowed by `|| true`) — closed.** The `pre-merge` spec-precedence check now captures `git log`'s own exit status via the errexit-safe `cmd || rc=$?` idiom, distinguishing a genuine git failure (now refuses, reusing the `not-a-git-repo` token, exit 2) from the legitimate "no commit has touched this path yet" empty-output case (still correctly skipped). Fixture added: a board naming an invalid-pathspec-magic spec path (`:(bogus)notreal.md`, verified live: `git log ... -- ':(bogus)notreal.md'` exits 128 with "fatal: Invalid pathspec magic") — refuses exit 2 rather than silently skipping the precedence check.

**Minor 2 (`date=` never validated) — closed.** `date=` is now validated against `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$` (the record grammar's own documented shape), refusing `approval-malformed` on a shape violation. Fixture added: `date=not-a-date` refuses.

**Provenance.** All six fixes and the design choices behind each (regex bound width, token reuse vs. new tokens, the parser's algorithm, the message's replacement locator) are recorded as decision/reason/grounding triples in `.shell-team/provenance/T-1103.md` (appended, 6 new entries; 13 total; `bash bin/check-provenance.sh .shell-team/provenance/T-1103.md` → `conformant`). The file's FIRST pre-existing decision (the original greedy-`sed` extraction design) is explicitly marked superseded by the new field-extraction decision rather than left standing uncorrected.

The `pre-merge` branch's `APPROVES` (`^[0-9a-f]{40}$`) never enters arithmetic (compared and passed to `git` as a string), so it carries no `10#` exposure at all.

**Fix (site 5): ported `bin/check-intent.sh`'s own `{1,4}`-digit bound.** `bin/check-intent.sh:428`–`:440`'s `HASH_FULL_RE` bounds the identical `- intent-hash (v<M>):` version field to `{1,4}` digits, with a comment citing **T-1021 (D4, Codex round1 Major)** by name as the reason. Ported verbatim (with the citation) rather than reusing `APPROVES`'s own `{1,15}` bound, so both operands of the *same* equality now share one digit-width ceiling for what DP-13 already declares a class-blind version count — removing an asymmetry rather than introducing one. New split: `HASH_LOOSE_RE` (`^[[:space:]]*-\ intent-hash\ \(`, "is this an intent-hash sub-bullet at all") and `HASH_STRICT_RE` (`^[[:space:]]*-\ intent-hash\ \(v([0-9]{1,4})\):\ [0-9a-f]{40}$`, the bounded full grammar) — the same loose/strict pairing `check-intent.sh` already uses (`HASH_LINE_RE`/`HASH_FULL_RE`).

**Refusal semantics chosen: fail-closed, exit 1, new token, never echoing the digits.** A line matching the loose anchor but failing the bounded strict grammar is board content this checker cannot evaluate — it now refuses `intent-hash-malformed` (a NEW token, since it names a different board line than the approval record itself) at **exit 1** (the same "content refusal" class every other malformed-grammar refusal in this file already uses — not exit 2, since this is committed board content failing a grammar, not a "cannot even attempt evaluation" class), rather than being silently skipped-and-excluded from the `MAXV` count. Skip-and-continue was rejected on purpose: it would let a fabricated oversized (or otherwise malformed) intent-hash line hide the board's real maximum from the equality instead of being counted against it — exactly the failure mode the mandate named. This mirrors `check-intent.sh`'s own disposition for the identical shape: a line matching `HASH_LINE_RE` but not `HASH_FULL_RE` increments `hash_bad_count`, which unconditionally fails the check (`fail_hash_structural`) rather than dropping the line from the count. The refusal message names the task and the sub-bullet SHAPE only, never the offending digit string or any other byte of the malformed line (per the mandate's explicit instruction).

This is parity-**with-a-guard** rather than a verbatim substitution of the sibling `RE_HOME_PATH_RAW`'s own `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`: a verbatim substitution would admit a bare separator run (`-Users---`) as a false positive (the class would happily consume a trailing hyphen as "the name" and the next as the closing separator), which is exactly the interaction risk the review itself named. **Codex review round 1 (2026-08-26): `REQUEST_CHANGES`** — `READY_FOR_REVIEW` -> `READY_FOR_ENG`. Record: `.shell-team/reviews/T-1099.md`. One **Blocker** and one **Major**, both in the new structural-heading assertion's OTHER-bucket identity encoding, both independently reproduced against the real script before being trusted: **(Blocker)** two bare `##` headings (empty normalized identity) silently passed the at-most-once rule — `log_heading("OTHER", "")` wrote a bare `OTHER` token with no tab, the read-side `awk -F'\t' '$1=="OTHER"{print $2}'` printed an empty string for each occurrence, `uniq -d` could only report the duplicate as a single blank line, and bash command substitution strips an all-blank-lines result down to the empty string — so `[ -n "$other_dupes" ]` never fired, defeating AC8's fail-closed mechanism on a heading form (bare `##`) the spec's own Input space names reachable (class 6). **(Major)** two textually distinct headings sharing a prefix up to an internal literal tab (`## Foo<TAB>Bar` vs `## Foo<TAB>Baz`) were falsely flagged as duplicates, because `awk -F'\t'` field-splits on every tab and the read-side truncated the identity at its own first internal tab — contradicting decision (b)'s "internal whitespace preserved literally." One Minor (embedded-NUL-byte variant of the same truncation class) was downgraded and dispositioned **won't-fix** by the reviewer's own ground: out of the spec's declared Input space ("an honest-error tool, not an adversarial-input parser").

**Engineer rework round 1 (2026-08-26): fixed the ENCODING, not the symptom, per the reviewer's own instruction.** Both findings share one root cause — an unsafe single-byte (`\t`) read-side extraction of a possibly-empty or possibly-tab-containing identity, returned to bash as a bare string tested for emptiness — so one redesign closes both. **New encoding, in two lines**: (1) every OTHER heading is logged as `OTHER<TAB><byte-length-of-identity><TAB><identity>` (`bin/check-board-headings.sh`'s `log_heading()`), so an empty identity is `OTHER\t0\t` — never a bare, strippable token; (2) the entire duplicate JUDGMENT (not just field extraction) now runs inside ONE awk pass over an associative array keyed by the identity reconstructed via `substr($0, length($1)+1+length($2)+1+1)` — a BYTE-OFFSET read, never a re-split on tab — so the only thing that ever crosses back into bash is a guaranteed non-blank `DUP<TAB><display>` report line (with an explicit `(blank heading)` placeholder for a duplicated empty identity), and presence is decided by `grep -c '^DUP'` (a line count), never by a `[ -n ... ]` test on a substituted string. Per-finding fix: **Blocker** — the length prefix makes an empty identity a real, non-blank, countable record, and the duplicate decision is made inside awk (never returned to bash as a possibly-blank string). **Major** — the identity is located by byte offset past the tag+length fields, never by re-splitting the record on tab, so an internal tab in the identity can no longer be mistaken for a field boundary. Won't-fix (embedded NUL) left untouched, per the reviewer's own disposition.

**Class closed — identity-representation edge set enumerated and fixtured** (all reachable per the spec's Input space): empty (`t1099-bare-dup-head.md`/`t1099-bare-single-head.md`, the Blocker's own case plus its at-most-once positive control), whitespace-only (`t1099-whitespace-only-dup-head.md`, normalizes to the same empty identity as a bare `##` and must collide with it), internal tab (`t1099-internal-tab-distinct-head.md`/`t1099-internal-tab-identical-head.md`, the Major's own case plus its identical-including-tab positive control), very long (`t1099-long-single-head.md`/`t1099-long-dup-head.md`, a 500-byte identity — no truncation, no crash), and trailing-spaces-pre-normalization (`t1099-trailing-ws-dup-head.md`, `## Format` vs `## Format   ` still collide once trimmed). 8 new fixtures, wired into `tests/check-board-headings/run.sh` as one new `T-1099 identity-encoding` case plus two new inline counterfactuals (`T-1099 dup-done counterfactual` / `T-1099 dup-active counterfactual`, each a frozen, self-contained, byte-verbatim copy of the OLD write+read pair reproducing the Blocker and the Major respectively — never a moving git ref).

### Engineer rework (round 3, bounded final fix round — operator-ruled option A, 2026-08-23), review record `.shell-team/reviews/T-1092.md` `## Round 2` — flag stays `REWORK`, pending re-review

**Blocker 1 (heading-boundary asymmetry) — fixed.** `bin/close-out.sh`'s round-2 fix paired an EXACT heading search (`grep -n '^## Spec review$'`) with a LOOSE boundary check (`awk`'s `/^## /`): a later round's heading carrying a trailing-whitespace deviation (the reviewer's repro: one trailing space) was invisible to the search but visible to the boundary, so the scan anchored to an earlier, well-formed round and stopped right before the malformed later one — never reading its REQUEST_CHANGES at all. Rewritten as ONE `awk` pass, ONE discipline: the heading search now trims trailing whitespace before the equality test (so `## Spec review ` / `## Spec review<TAB>` still count as a genuine round heading), while the boundary check keeps its original loose `/^## /` test against the untrimmed line. A genuinely different section (e.g. a later default-mode `## Round N`) still does not trim-equal the canonical heading and is correctly excluded from the search — this was evaluated and is why the alternative "loosen the search to `/^## /` too, extract to EOF" design was rejected: a real review record's `## Spec review` section is followed, after the whole loop completes, by the default mode's own later round headings, and that alternative would incorrectly re-scope onto them (see provenance).
- New fixture `tests/close-out/run.sh` `T-99517`: the reviewer's own two-round repro (round 1 exact `## Spec review` / APPROVE, round 2 `## Spec review ` with one trailing space / REQUEST_CHANGES) → refuses.

**Blocker 2 (pipefail×SIGPIPE false refusal) — fixed.** The verdict match `printf '%s\n' "$LATEST_SECTION" | grep -qE '...'` is racy under `set -o pipefail`: `grep -q` exits on its first match without draining its input, a large `$LATEST_SECTION` can leave `printf` still writing when `grep` closes the pipe, `printf` receives SIGPIPE, and the pipeline's own reported status goes non-zero even though `grep` genuinely matched — falsely refusing a valid APPROVE. Replaced with a here-string (`grep -qE '...' <<< "$LATEST_SECTION"`), which reads the same content with no separate writer process and therefore no pipe for a SIGPIPE to travel across. Chose the here-string over the reviewer's other suggested option (folding the match into the extraction's own `awk` pass) to keep the two concerns — which lines belong to the latest round; does that content contain an exact APPROVE — as two separately-readable, separately-tested statements, matching this gate's existing per-check style (see provenance).
- New fixture `tests/close-out/run.sh` `T-99518`: a ~200KB `## Spec review` section (100KB filler before and after the verdict line, via `head -c 100000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'x'`) carrying a genuinely valid, exactly-matching APPROVE → still passes.

Fixed: the parenthetical now states the three readers share the same *design pattern* (a pre-intent-hash hand-off field, cross-checked against the matching Routing-Map decision), not the same field, and names which field each of the other two actually keys off; the paragraph now states both failure shapes explicitly — (1) a mismatch, unchanged from round 1; (2) an unreadable `- entry-mode:` value (missing/duplicated/out-of-vocabulary) fails closed and refuses the route-back, routing to `pm-spec`, never assumed `pm-authored` by default — mirroring the Conformance-read confirmation gate's own already-reviewed language for this exact field. Widened `bin/close-out.sh`'s normalization to collapse every whitespace run (leading/internal/trailing) to a single space before the equality test, closing the whole whitespace-variance class rather than the one reported position; new fixture `T-99519` (QA's exact repro) refuses, mutation-probed on a scratch worktree (`/tmp/claude-502/t1092-mutwt-parent/mut4`, removed after — reverting the widened normalization alone flips `T-99519` red, restored green); `bash tests/close-out/run.sh` → 110 PASS / 0 FAIL / 19 `PASS: T-1092`; `check-acs` 20/0/1, `check-intent` aligned v1, `check-prompt-sync`/`check-handoff` exit 0, `shellcheck` clean on all three suites, `.shell-team/provenance/T-1092.md` now 10 decision entries conformant, `git status --short` clean after commit. Flag stays `REWORK`.

**Design fix (operator-ruled option A, third ruling on this component, 2026-08-23, `.shell-team/interventions/T-1092.md` fourth entry) — what the old design was, why it kept leaking, what the new invariant is.** The old design (rounds 3 and 3.1): the SELECTOR ("is this line THE `## Spec review` heading") was progressively normalized across two rounds (exact-match → trailing-trim → collapse-all-whitespace-then-trim), but the BOUNDARY ("is this OTHER line A heading at all, i.e. where does the latest section end") kept reading the RAW, unnormalized line the whole time (`raw[i] ~ /^## /`). Every round's fix therefore widened only one side of a two-sided comparison — three rounds found three different byte patterns (an exact-vs-loose split, then a trailing-whitespace variant, then an internal-whitespace variant) where the two sides disagreed, and QA round 4 found a fourth, in the dangerous direction this time: a later, genuinely unrelated heading indented with LEADING whitespace (`  ## Some Other Section`) was invisible to the raw boundary regex (it doesn't start with `#`), so the extraction silently leaked PAST it, and a stray `### Codex Spec-Review verdict: APPROVE` line sitting in that leaked, unrelated content produced a false PASS on a record whose true latest round was `REQUEST_CHANGES`. **The new invariant**: every line is normalized exactly once into one value (`normv[i]` — collapse every whitespace run to a single space, trim both ends), and BOTH judgments now read that same normalized value — the boundary is `normv[i] ~ /^## /`, the selector is `normv[i] == "## Spec review"`. One discipline cannot disagree with itself: there is no longer a "boundary sees a heading, selector doesn't" or "selector sees THE heading, boundary doesn't" byte pattern left to discover, because there is only one view of each line remaining to check against. The only residual is the normalization's own completeness, and that is bounded to whitespace by construction — a heading differing from `## Spec review` by anything other than whitespace amount/position (different words, wrong case, extra text) still correctly fails both judgments. **Design fix A2 (operator-ruled, fourth ruling on this component, 2026-08-23, `.shell-team/interventions/T-1092.md` fifth entry) — the three-way disposition, and why the CR strip discharges the frozen CR-tolerance declaration.** QA round 5 found the single-normalization design (the prior "Design fix" paragraph above) closed the boundary/selector divergence class structurally, but the whole-file FALLBACK was still a single, ambiguous rule: "if `last` was never set, use the whole file." That rule conflated two genuinely different record shapes — a record with no heading structure at all (the correct, intended target: AC6's own bare-verdict fixture) and a record whose heading DETECTION failed for some other reason (a bug: the whole-file scan can then find a verdict-shaped line anywhere, including a stale earlier round). A CRLF-terminated record hit the second case: `awk`'s default record separator is `\n` only, so every line's trailing `\r` survived as the LAST character of `$0`, no heading line could ever normalize to exactly `## Spec review`, `last` stayed `0`, the fallback fired, and a stale round-1 APPROVE survived a genuinely later REQUEST_CHANGES — a false PASS that also contradicted this spec's own frozen `## Input space` declaration naming "the CR-tolerant variant the existing tooling handles" as a handled input, not a Non-input synthetic extreme. **Two changes discharge that declaration for real rather than disclaiming it**: (1) a per-line `sub(/\r$/, "", $0)` strip runs FIRST, before any other processing, on the line stored into `raw[]` too — so a CRLF file's headings normalize identically to an LF file's, and the content later handed to the verdict grep is already CR-free (the verdict anchor's own `$` could otherwise be defeated by a trailing `\r` exactly as the heading match was — reasoned through and fixed, not just the heading half of the bug); the bash-side whole-file fallback path is CR-stripped the same way (`tr -d '\r'`), so CR-tolerance holds uniformly across every disposition, not only the awk-side extraction. (2) The fallback is split into a **three-way disposition**, tracked by one boolean (`any_heading`) alongside the existing `last`: **(a) has-target-section** (`last != 0`) — extract the latest round exactly as before; **(b) no-headings-at-all** (`last == 0 && any_heading == 0`, awk exit 1) — the record genuinely has no section structure, so the whole-file scan this fallback exists for is exactly right, unchanged from round 1's own design; **(c) headings-but-no-target** (`last == 0 && any_heading != 0`, awk exit 2) — the record has section structure but none of it is a Spec review round, so an elected task's teeth REFUSE rather than fall back to a scan that could pick up an unrelated stray verdict-shaped line sitting in ordinary body text (the fail-closed reading: no APPROVE in an actual Spec review section means no APPROVE, full stop). Bash captures both non-zero awk exit codes explicitly via `if VAR=$(cmd); then …; else RC=$?; fi` (never `|| true`, which would erase the very distinction this fix exists to draw). New fixtures: `T-99521` (QA's exact CRLF repro, multi-round, refuses), `T-99522` (a CRLF-terminated record whose latest round is genuinely APPROVE, a positive control, passes), `T-99523` (headings exist — `## Notes` — but no `## Spec review` section, plus a stray APPROVE-shaped line in the body, refuses); `T-99501` (the bare-verdict, no-headings shape) reconfirmed still passing through the narrowed fallback. `bash tests/close-out/run.sh` → 114 PASS / 0 FAIL / 23 `PASS: T-1092`, zero existing fixtures edited or dropped. Two mutation probes on a scratch worktree (`/tmp/claude-502/t1092-mutwt-parent/mut6`, removed after): (a) reverting the CR strip alone (keeping the disambiguation intact) flips `T-99522` red, restored green — **`T-99521` was independently checked under this same isolated mutation and did NOT flip**, staying correctly refused, because the disambiguation clause independently classifies a record whose only headings fail to CR-normalize as "headings-but-no-target" and refuses on that separate basis; reported as an observed defense-in-depth overlap between the two clauses rather than forced to match a predicted-both-flip outcome. (b) reverting the fallback disambiguation alone (keeping the CR strip intact) flips `T-99523` red, restored green. `check-acs` 20/0/1, AC5 individually PASS, `check-intent` aligned v1 (unchanged hash — no drift), `bash tests/codex-skeleton-hygiene/run.sh` → 40 PASS / 0 FAIL, `check-prompt-sync`/`check-handoff`/`check-board-headings`/`check-pii-shapes` all exit 0, `shellcheck` clean on all three suites, `.shell-team/provenance/T-1092.md` now 12 decision entries conformant, `git status --short` clean after commit. Flag stays `REWORK`.

**Item-1/2 adversarial probes, independently run against the real `bin/close-out.sh`** (fresh scratch dir, all four env redirections):
- (a) reviewer's exact repro — round 1 exact `## Spec review` heading + APPROVE, round 2 `## Spec review ` (one trailing space) heading + REQUEST_CHANGES → **refused** (`elected spec review has no APPROVE verdict`). Matches `T-99517` and the review's own reproduction exactly.
- (b) trailing-TAB variant of the same shape → **refused**, same sentinel. The trim-based heading search correctly treats a trailing tab the same as a trailing space (both stripped by `sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", trimmed)`).
- (c) ordinary two-round answered-then-approved flow (earlier REQUEST_CHANGES, later exact-heading APPROVE) → **passed silently** (rc=0). No regression on the well-formed case.
- **(d) my own creative variant, as requested: `##  Spec review` (double space between `##` and `Spec`, not trailing) as the later, REQUEST_CHANGES-carrying round, following an exact-heading APPROVE round.** Observed: **passed silently (rc=0)** — the task closes out even though its true latest round is REQUEST_CHANGES. Root cause, read directly from the shipped `awk` script: the heading *search* only trims **trailing** whitespace (`sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", trimmed)`) before comparing to the literal `"## Spec review"`; a double space **between** `##` and `Spec` survives that trim unchanged and is not trim-equal to the canonical heading, so the search never advances past the earlier, well-formed round. The boundary check (`raw[i] ~ /^## /`, unchanged from round 2) *does* recognize the malformed line as a section boundary, so the scan correctly stops extracting right before it — but that just means the malformed later round's own content, including its REQUEST_CHANGES, is silently invisible rather than differently handled. **This is the identical asymmetry class Blocker 1 (round 2) was fixed to close, reoccurring on a different byte pattern the round-3 fix's scope did not cover** (the fix comment and the provenance record both frame the fix as addressing "trailing whitespace" specifically, not whitespace anywhere in the heading). Given the round-2 review's own precedent for judging this class of finding ("a stray trailing space... is ordinary, plausible imprecision," not a synthetic extreme), a stray internal double space is the same kind of ordinary imprecision and is equally reachable from real LLM-authored output. **Not treated as a round-3 gating FAIL**, for three reasons stated plainly rather than silently: (1) it is outside the four items the operator's bounded-final-fix ruling (option A) explicitly scoped this round to; (2) the coordinator's own round-3 brief asked this probe to be run and its outcome *reported*, not treated as a new fix requirement; (3) it does not violate any of the spec's 20 `- check:` criteria (none of AC1–AC20 exercises internal-whitespace heading malformation) nor any shipped fixture. No regression.

**A defect found and fixed during this task's own AC9(a) construction, disclosed rather than folded away.** While building the worked determinism demonstration below, this role noticed the region defined the closed ordinal set (`full`, `partial`, `absent`) and anchored each value, but never stated **which value outranks which** for the `comparison` rule to actually apply at those three ranks — an omission the Verdict scope's own item 1 (`a comparison that leaves two distinct vectors incomparable`) names as an in-scope Major. Fixed in commit `aff1265`, before hand-off: one explicit sentence fixing `full > partial > absent` for all three ordinal criteria, plus a second finding surfaced by the same exercise — `ac-pass-completeness` is a pure eligibility gate rather than a discriminator once the `floor` has been applied, since every floor-eligible candidate necessarily reads the oracle's own maximum (`11 passed, 0 failed` — the only value the exit-`0` floor admits), so the comparison in practice starts deciding at rank 2 among floor-eligible candidates. Neither finding is grep-checkable (no `- check:` line asserts an ordering direction), so this is exactly the class of substance defect `## Verdict scope` prices to a human read rather than to a guard — caught here by actually working the mechanism rather than by narrating it.

**AC9, item by item.**

**(a) Worked determinism demonstration — three vectors, each labelled a worked example, no fabricated candidate artifacts, no `- judge-pick:` line in any form.**

*Example 1 — rank 1 ties (both floor-eligible), rank 2 decides.* Candidate-01: `ac-pass-completeness` = 11 passed, 0 failed (floor met — `acceptance.sh` exits `0`); `test-depth` = `full`; `scope-discipline` = `full`; `hygiene` = `full`. Candidate-02: `ac-pass-completeness` = 11 passed, 0 failed (floor met — identical to Candidate-01, confirming the gate-not-discriminator finding above); `test-depth` = `partial`; `scope-discipline` = `full`; `hygiene` = `absent`. Resolution: rank 1 (`ac-pass-completeness`) — 11/0 equals 11/0, ties, no decision. Rank 2 (`test-depth`) — `full` outranks `partial` (per the ranking-order sentence above): **Candidate-01 wins**, ranks 3–4 never consulted. Disposition: `pick`, candidate-01.

*Example 2 — every rank ties, both tie-break steps exercised in order.* Candidate-01 and Candidate-03 both score identically: 11 passed/0 failed, `full`, `full`, `full` — every one of the four ranks ties, so the `comparison` rule alone cannot decide. Tie-break step 1 (earliest completed check results): in this worked scenario both candidates' check results are recorded as completing at the identical timestamp (a legitimate tie at this step too, not assumed away), so step 1 does not decide either. Tie-break step 2 (lexicographically lowest candidate id): under the `candidate-id-grammar` (`candidate-NN`), `candidate-01` sorts lexicographically before `candidate-03` (first two bytes `ca` identical throughout the common prefix, the differing byte `1` < `3`) — **Candidate-01 wins** by the grammar's own totality. Disposition: `pick`, candidate-01.

*Example 3 — every candidate below the floor, resolves to `none`.* Candidate-04: `acceptance.sh` reports 9 passed, 2 failed, exit `1` — below the floor, ineligible for `pick` regardless of its other three scores. Candidate-05: `acceptance.sh` reports 7 passed, 4 failed, exit `1` — likewise ineligible. No candidate in this firing clears the floor. Resolution: per `none-disposition`, the judge records `disposition: none`, the per-criterion scores of both considered candidates (for audit — a real judge would still record what it saw, even though nothing was pickable), and a rationale stating that no candidate cleared the floor. At N=2 this yields no `tier2-rework-rounds-avoided` datapoint for this firing, exactly as the region's own `none-disposition` line discloses.

**New line-241-equivalent replacement (the review's cited line, now at line 245 after the amendment's earlier insertions shifted it), quoted verbatim:**
> a **declared label**: the orchestrator's own launch parameter, recorded as passed, for every instance in the arms that actually created an instance (`plugin-role-n2`, `plugin-role-n4`; `launch-refused` created no instance at all and is excluded from that count — `## Probe evidence` above, "Arm: launch-refused"). This is not harness-originated evidence of the *resolved* type: the span rows' `"span"` field and the launch record's `- assign:` ids quoted in `## Probe evidence` above are the orchestrator's own attribution labels, and are deliberately not cited here as type evidence — the citable ground for this line is the epistemic-status paragraph added to `## Probe evidence` above ("Arm: launch-refused"). T-1058's declared-not-observed doctrine and T-1073's own recording of `subagent_type=general-purpose` are cited here only as grounds for treating this value as a declared label and for the recording practice itself — never as evidence that the declaration is true.

**⚠ Finding — Blocker, sends this round to REWORK.** `bin/check-fanout-instances.sh`'s `--telemetry` precondition check (`[ -r "$TELEMETRY" ]`) accepts a **directory** path — a directory passes bash's `-r` test — and the script then proceeds to `done < "$TELEMETRY"` in Phase 1's row-selection loop. Reading from a directory fails inside the `read` builtin with an **uncontrolled bash engine message on stderr**, and the script falls through to the exit-3 `no-rows` path rather than refusing at the invocation-check stage. This is a reachable input this task's own `## Input space` explicitly declares in scope ("Missing, empty and unreadable inputs at either path") — not a synthetic extreme — and a directory is a very plausible real-world mistake here specifically (e.g. an operator passing `bin/team-paths.sh --get runs`'s own directory output instead of the `<loop_id>.jsonl` file inside it). It breaks the frozen Goal paragraph's own explicit contract, verbatim: *"On every non-zero exit stdout is empty and exactly one classified line ... reaches stderr."* Reproduction (own scratch fixtures, real producers):
```
$ mkdir -p "$T/adir"
$ bash bin/check-fanout-instances.sh --telemetry "$T/adir" --run-id QR1 --phase implement --aggregation "$T/agg" --label qazi
bin/check-fanout-instances.sh: line 352: read: read error: 0: Is a directory
check-fanout-instances: no-rows: the declared scope (run_id=QR1 phase=implement) selected zero span rows
$ echo $?
3
```
Observed: stdout empty (0 lines, correct); **stderr carries 2 lines** (`grep -c . "$T/dir3.err"` → `2`), not 1 — the uncontrolled `read: read error: 0: Is a directory` line plus the classified `no-rows` line. Expected, per the frozen Goal: stdout empty AND exactly one classified stderr line. Additionally, `no-rows` (an *incomplete-fan-out* class whose declared remedy is "re-run or re-emit the missing assignment") is the wrong classification for what is actually an invocation-level defect (a directory is not a valid telemetry file) — `usage`/exit 2 is the correct class here, by the same reasoning AC7 already applies to a *nonexistent* `--telemetry` path. Confirmed this is a real gap, not shared by the sibling tool this spec explicitly says to model: `bin/aggregate-verdicts.sh --population <a directory>` handles the identical shape cleanly (`aggregate-verdicts: empty-population: population file has no entries: ...`, exactly 1 stderr line, correctly classified) — own run, reproduced live. No `- check:` line in the spec exercises a directory-shaped path (all AC7 usage-surface fixtures use a nonexistent path, `"$T/nope.jsonl"`, never an existing directory), which is why the mechanical sweep above is clean while this defect is real.
- **Suggested fix (for the engineer, not prescribed as the only shape):** add `[ -f "$TELEMETRY" ] || die 2 usage "--telemetry path is not a regular file: $TELEMETRY"` alongside the existing `[ -r "$TELEMETRY" ]` check (and consider the same for `--aggregation`, for defensive symmetry, even though that path currently happens to degrade cleanly via the `2>/dev/null`-suppressed `grep`).
- **Not exempted by the Input-space rule:** this trigger (an unreadable/wrong-shaped path) is explicitly named as reachable in the spec's own `## Input space`, not a synthetic extreme the spec puts out of scope — the exemption does not apply.
- **Scope of the fix, per the pre-commitment's own classification:** this affects only the invocation-precondition surface, not the "never dropped" telemetry-side properties (presence/grammar/uniqueness) or the fail-closed exit-code/empty-stdout contract in general (which held correctly across every other adversarial fixture I tried, including six independently-built failure classes plus the vocabulary-collision control above) — a scoped craft fix, not evidence the design premise is broken.

  - source: issue **#203** (the epic; design point 4) is the design canon. **No new issue was filed for the task itself**: #203 is the tracker item and this is a slice of its stated scope, so a second would duplicate it. Sprint v2.0.0 feature task 6. Branch `feature/1058-telemetry`; PR base `develop`. This branch is **stacked on five predecessors** — T-1053 → T-1054 → T-1055 → T-1056 → T-1057 — so the merge base is `develop`'s tip and all five earlier tasks' delivered paths are already changed against it through no act of this task.
  - the problem in one sentence: T-1057 resolves each role's executor (provider / model / effort / adapter) immediately before invoking it and then **throws the answer away** — only `model` reaches a span row — so the cross-provider review invariant that `CLAUDE.md` states and `templates/binding-default.conf` ships as a default is **unfalsifiable after the fact**, and the four error classes `templates/task-envelope.txt` says exist "because #203 design point 4 names them as telemetry T-1057 needs ready" have nothing recording against them.
  - the deliverable, in one sentence: three nullable span flags on `bin/log-run.sh` (`--provider`, `--effort`, `--adapter`, recorded as three keys **appended after `parent_span_id`**), the same three learned as span-only keys by `bin/check-run.sh`, a per-reviewer-span provider relation **derived** by `bin/rollup-runs.sh` and stored nowhere, and one new canonical prompt block registered `contain` against both skills — plus fixtures in the three existing suites and a recipe entry. **No new script, no new suite, no CI change** (measured: `.github/workflows/check-handoff.yml` L29 already lists all three scripts and all three suites, and each suite already has its own step).
  - **the design decisions worth stating on the board**: (1) **`probe_kind` is declined** — it is a static property of the provider token compiled into the resolver's own table, so recording it per row would put a second copy of a fixed mapping into every log line, and no part of the relation needs it. (2) **`--effort -` records JSON `null`** — `-` is the binding grammar's only "no value" spelling and `null` is the row grammar's spelling for the same fact (measured: `bin/check-binding.sh` L364 exempts `effort` and no other field), so the writer maps one to the other rather than admitting two spellings or losing a whole row to a sentinel the resolver legitimately prints. (3) **no `error-class` field and no join** — the envelope declares **four** classes and the resolver refuses with **five** tokens and the sets differ in both directions (`usage`/`binding-unresolved` have no class, `invocation-failed` has no token), so freezing a join would be a second implementation of a vocabulary neither file owns; a refusal is recorded as its token verbatim in a field that is already free text. (4) **a refused phase writes no span at all** — a span is defined as one call into a sub-agent and the resolver refuses *before* anything is invoked, so the refusal is recorded with the **existing** `--event gate` id and the token as its `--label`, minting no event id, no status value and no field, and disturbing no count. (5) **the norm is a second prompt block, appended, not an edit to T-1057's** — a stated departure from the routing map's step list: editing `executor-resolution.md` reopens T-1057's AC11 content lock for a duty that is not resolution, and a second block keeps both skills' edits a **pure append**, which the run surface's already-spent AC17 line budget makes mandatory rather than tidy.
  - **DP6, the role-pair definition — where the design weight sits, answered without a cardinality-one assumption**: the **reviewer role set** is `{codex-reviewer}` and the **authoring role set** is `{engineer}`, each stated as a set with its membership reason (a review reads the diff the implementation produced; a spec and a design are inputs, not the artifact under review), keyed on the row's **`span`** field rather than `phase` because `span` names the role the relation is defined over. Scope is one `run_id` and the **nearest preceding authoring span in input order** — not the whole run, because a fifth review round is a statement about the fifth implementation round, and not `iteration`, because a rework round's two spans are not guaranteed to share one. Output is **one token per reviewer span**, never a per-run boolean: read against T-1055's real history of **five** review rounds in one task, a per-run boolean would have to pick one of five answers. Outcomes are a closed three — `cross-provider` | `same-provider` | `undetermined` — with `undetermined` **fail-closed** for every unknown (either side records no provider, no authoring span precedes, or the rows predate this task) and never `false`; and `same-provider` is a **legitimate reachable outcome**, not a defect report, since a host may legally bind both roles to one provider.
  - **pre-commitment, with the drop order and the never-dropped set both named before round 1**: factual trigger = two consecutive rework rounds of new independent `Blocker`/`Major` findings against one component; contextual = a third round about to start; **the factual trigger governs when they disagree** (repo default, not loosened). **Never dropped**: ① telemetry stays best-effort and never blocks the loop (nothing written on a validation refusal, every caller keeps `|| true`, the roll-up exits 0 over any population), ② two-generation fail-closed (a row with no binding never yields `same-provider` or `cross-provider`, no key becomes required, every existing log stays valid) and ③ `bin/resolve-executor.sh` keeps its zero write path (the row travels as flags in the orchestrator's own context — no state file, no env var, not even as a test seam). If a round's findings would require **weakening** any of the three, the task **stops and returns to sprint planning** — no fourth droppable is invented to avoid the stop.   - **the design decisions worth stating on the board**: (1) **a model sentinel is not expressible, measured rather than assumed** — `bin/check-binding.sh`'s `MODEL_RE` requires a leading alphanumeric, so a bare `-` in the model column is refused `bad-token` and only `effort` has a "no value" spelling; the shipped default's `codex-reviewer` row therefore carries the ordinary token `provider-configured`, whose meaning the file's header states, rather than this machine's Codex configuration (which would encode one host's setup into every adopter's default). (2) **the `claude-cli` "available by construction" question is answered rather than skipped** — probing a `claude` binary on `PATH` would measure a *different object* (a CLI installation, absent while the harness runs fine and present while it cannot spawn a sub-agent), so the resolver makes no claim it cannot ground: the probe table declares the kind, and the canonical block places the in-process duty where the observation exists — the caller treats the harness's own invocation failure as `executor-unavailable`. A provider with **no table entry at all** is unavailable, never assumed available, which is what stops a future third adapter inheriting availability by omission. (3) **the frontmatter pins' retirement rests on a premise pm-spec cannot measure**, so DP6 pre-decides both branches: if the harness accepts a per-invocation model, the five `claude-cli` pins retire; if it does not, they stay and a two-directional pin↔default equality lock ships instead, with retirement deferred to an issue. Branch `feature/1056-loop-liveness`; PR base `develop`. This branch is **stacked three deep** — on T-1055's tip, which is on T-1054's, which is on T-1053's — so the merge base is `develop`'s tip and all three earlier tasks' delivered paths are already changed against it through no act of this task.
  - the deliverable, in one sentence: four new files — `bin/check-liveness.sh` (a fail-closed classifier read out-of-band by a timer this task does not ship, emitting exactly one bare token on stdout — `RUNNING` / `WAITING` / `STALLED` / `DEAD` / `OBSERVE_ERROR` at exits 0/3/4/5/2 — from a closed 19-token refusal set), `tests/check-liveness/run.sh`, `templates/liveness-reasons.txt` (the closed 8-row reason vocabulary a declaration draws from) and `templates/prompt-blocks/liveness-declaration.md` (the write/clear norm authored once, registered `contain` against both skills) — plus one registry row, one choke-point paragraph appended to each of `skills/run/SKILL.md` and `skills/goal/SKILL.md`, CI wiring and a test-recipe append. **Nothing consumes the verdict**: no transport, no daemon, no loop gate, no board write.
  - **the design decisions worth stating on the board**: (1) **exit `1` is assigned to no verdict at all** — bash's own `errexit` fallback is 1, so a contract that used it could not distinguish "decided this" from "crashed before deciding", and a behavioural assertion over it would be structurally vacuous. (2) **`STALLED` and `DEAD` are not separated by a distinction of kind, and the spec says so** — nothing in already-persisted state, read read-only, reports whether a process is alive, and the issue rules out the loop writing its own heartbeat. What separates them is a second threshold **plus a second quantity**: `DEAD` requires the tick clock *and* the last-commit clock both past `T_dead`, so it is strictly stronger than a bigger number on one clock. (3) **The board's active flags are declined as a matrix dimension and read by nothing** — a flag names which phase a task is in, never whether anything is executing, so classifying on it would repeat the stillness-as-alarm error the issue rejects one level up; the classifier resolves no board path. (4) **A missed deletion cannot pin `WAITING` forever** — the failure mode that would make the artifact worse than nothing is closed structurally rather than by discipline: a declaration whose `run-epoch` differs from the run's `start_epoch` is refused, and one whose `declared-epoch` is not later than the state file's mtime is *superseded* (the loop demonstrably ticked since the wait was declared) and falls through to the ladder, whose `RUNNING` cell independently requires that same recent mtime.
  - **DP4's omission class is closed by a mechanism, not a sweep**: 17 human-hand-off points across the two skills are enumerated with line numbers in the spec, and rather than 17 individual edits the design is **one choke point per skill plus one closed reason vocabulary**, with `bin/check-prompt-sync.sh` enforcing that neither surface drifts from the canonical block and a two-directional set equality enforcing that no skill invents a reason the classifier will refuse and no registry row exists with no writer.

If a round's findings would require **weakening** either, the task **stops and returns to sprint planning** rather than being patched — it is not silently dropped and no third droppable is invented to avoid the stop. Droppable, in order: **(1) the second threshold separating `DEAD` from `STALLED`** — collapse to three values, deleting `T_dead`, `--dead-after`, the last-commit conjunct, exit 5 and the `DEAD` cells; retained is the declared-wait distinction plus stall detection, which are the two halves #227 actually names, and what is lost, stated rather than argued away, is telling a wedged run from an abandoned one. **(2) the state-file half of the output** — delete `--out`, the verdict document and the `out-unwritable` token, leaving stdout as the only channel; a timer wanting to diff consecutive verdicts must then keep its own record.   - **M1 class inventory — every input this script reads in more than one step, each site's apply/not-apply decision (for QA/reviewer coverage audit):**
    1. **State file mtime + content — APPLY, fixed.** Replaced the single stat-then-awk read with a bounded consistency re-read: stat, read `start_epoch`/`iteration`, stat again; if the mtime moved, retry (up to 3 total attempts); the LAST (freshest) mtime observed is what feeds `A_STATE`. If it is still moving after the bound, that is itself evidence the loop is writing *right now* — the freshest sample still flows into the ladder's **one existing** `RUNNING` emit site (no second site added; `AC4`'s static count is unchanged at exactly 1, re-confirmed below).
    2. **Declaration file's read path — APPLY, fixed (narrower scope than #1).** Replaced a separate readability CHECK (`-r`) followed by a separate OPEN (`while read < path`) with one guarded `exec 3< "$path"` open, read from that held fd, then close — closing the check-then-open gap where the write/clear choke point could delete the file between the two. Once open, POSIX unlink-while-open semantics mean a concurrent delete can no longer truncate the read. What is explicitly **not** fixed and stated why: the WRITE side's atomicity (whether the choke point writes the declaration atomically) is outside this task's control — DP3's own format design (version-line-first, terminator-last, exact required fields) is what makes a torn read of a mid-write declaration self-evidently detectable, refused `declaration-malformed`/`declaration-unterminated` by the *existing* structural validators rather than silently accepted as valid.
    3. **`HEAD`'s resolution vs. its committer-epoch read — NOT-APPLY, cannot race.** `git log -1 --format=%ct HEAD` resolves the ref and reads the commit's committer epoch in ONE git invocation, not two separate steps — there is no window between "resolve HEAD" and "read its epoch" for anything to land in.
    4. **The `--out` target's occupancy check vs. the `mv` — NOT-APPLY, out of this task's declared scope.** A check-then-act gap exists in principle (the target could be replaced between the occupancy check and the `mv`), but the realistic actor is a single repeating timer invoking this script sequentially, never concurrently — the spec's own Non-goals name "concurrency between two classifier invocations writing the same `--out` path" as "the operator's arrangement, not an input class this deliverable accommodates", and the repository's trust boundary (`CLAUDE.md`'s security invariant; this checker's own header) treats the operator and working directory as trusted, not hostile. The occupancy-*type* half of this same site is M2's own finding, fixed below.

Two cases: `cl-race-shadow-noop-control-stalled` (the forwarding-only shadow changes nothing — a vacuity control proving the shadow mechanism itself is transparent) and `cl-race-shadow-touch-running` (the touching shadow lands the mutation mid-read; the classifier's bounded retry picks up the fresh mtime it produces and reports `RUNNING`, not the stale pre-touch one) — both verified against a real, unmodified `bin/check-liveness.sh`, no production hook involved in either.
  - **One flaky-test bug found and fixed while authoring the shadow technique, disclosed rather than silently patched away**: the first draft let the classifier compute its own `NOW` via `date +%s` internally, then compared it against the shadow's `touch` (which sets the file's mtime to REAL wall-clock time at the instant it fires, *after* the classifier already captured `NOW`). When the touch landed on a later wall-clock second than the classifier's own `NOW` sample — an ordinary, non-adversarial timing gap of a fraction of a second landing across a second boundary — the file's mtime became numerically *ahead* of `NOW`, and the classifier correctly (per DP5) refused `clock-skew` instead of reporting `RUNNING`. Measured directly: 2 failures in 5 consecutive runs before the fix, 0 failures in 18 consecutive runs after it. Fixed by capturing a single `$LIVENESS_NOW` once, with a 30-second forward buffer, and passing it explicitly to both shadow cases — removing the real-time race from the ASSERTION without touching the real-time race the shadow exists to reproduce inside the classifier's own reads.

  - the deliverable, in one sentence: four new files — `bin/check-binding.sh` (a line-oriented, never-sourced binding-config validator whose every refusal is one token from a closed 20-entry matrix with a fixed exit code, plus `--print-binding` / `--print-lock` / `--verify` integrity primitives sharing one normalization pipeline), `tests/check-binding/run.sh`, `templates/binding-adapters.txt` (the plugin-shipped adapter allowlist) and `templates/binding-template.conf` (the shipped specimen) — with CI wiring and a test-recipe append. Nothing consumes the binding: no agent, skill, adapter or phase transition reads it.
  - **the two design decisions worth stating on the board, both measured rather than assumed**: (1) **`bin/team-paths.sh` gains no key.** The config resolves as `<base>/binding.conf` composed from `--get base`, exactly as `bin/check-durability.sh` composes `<base>/durability-mode`. Measured ground: `tests/team-paths/run.sh:154-171` pins the resolver's key set at exactly ten in both directions and its own comment records T-1006's AC2 as having raised that pin from nine, so an eleventh key reddens that pin and the merged criteria behind it for a benefit nothing needs — the epic makes the config read-only to every agent, so no prompt-injected path is required. AC3 locks this as a negative criterion. (2) **the hash covers the canonical resolved binding, not the config's bytes** — a comment reflow, a row reorder or a CRLF conversion does not stop the loop, while any bound value change does. This deliberately narrows "a change is mechanically detected" to the property #203 actually protects; a stop triggered by a comment edit is a false stop that trains its reader to ignore it.
  - **where the integrity baseline lives, and what its independence rests on**: the recommended home is `<runs>/binding/<run-id>.lock` — under the resolver's `runs` key, which `templates/shell-team.gitignore` already marks as per-run, never-committed telemetry (measured), and a different directory from the config it describes. The load-bearing half is not the directory: the lock records the config path it was taken from and `--verify` **never re-resolves** that path, so a base directory resolving differently in a later phase is reported as `path-mismatch` instead of quietly followed. Nothing here creates that directory or mints a run id — that is T-1056's.
  - **stacked-branch scope note**: the diff base is `git merge-base develop HEAD`, which on this stacked branch is `develop`'s tip, **not** T-1053's tip — so T-1053's six delivered paths (`skills/run/SKILL.md`, `agents/pm-spec.md`, its spec and records) are already changed against that base through no act of this task. AC13's allow-list permits them as **pre-existing, not editable**; AC16(d) requires the executing side to measure whether T-1053's tip is an ancestor of `HEAD` and report it, and if it is not, the freeze stops rather than proceeds.

  - the decisions, in brief (D1–D10, full text in the spec's `### Settled decisions`). **D1 — the key is `<file>:<content>` and the judgment is declared count against measured count**, one mechanism producing both directions (`comm -23` forward, `comm -13` reverse) exactly as today. The alternative was rejected on a **measured decoy, not on taste**: a set difference over *deduplicated* content keys absorbs a second byte-identical unguarded line in the same file silently, which is strictly weaker than the position keying it would replace. An occurrence-index key reintroduces a position-like field that reorders on deletion; an anchor+content key needs an anchor that is a position pin under another name. **One derivation constraint is load-bearing**: the raw derivation keeps `grep -n`'s line numbers **through** its `sort -u` and strips them only when the key is formed — dropping the field earlier collapses two byte-identical sites at the source and no downstream count can recover them.   - the round-1 repair, in brief: **matchability is qualified rather than promised** — a merge SHA always matches, a pull-request number matches **only where the merge subjects actually carry one** (a merge-commit workflow writes it there, a squash or rebase workflow does not; stated that way to stay adopter-neutral), and a task ID **never appears in a sub-bullet at all** and is repositioned as the label the framing maps a SHA or PR number *from*, never a token the agent matches. Task IDs are **not** narrowed out of the Input space's framing-side list — the two texts are reconciled honestly instead, with a task-IDs-only framing declared a **reachable** input whose defined behaviour is the `## Notes` route. **Whole-window coverage is now part of the requirement**: every returned sub-bullet must end up matched to the cycle's own material or explicitly flagged as foreign, and the `## Notes` disposition now covers **both** failure modes (no matchable material, **and** any unaccounted or foreign entry). The `pr-metadata` stream is deliberately **not** joined to the reconciliation — it is optional and `gh`-auth-gated, so joining it would breach the fetch-nothing constraint that keeps the norm satisfiable in an adopter's repository. AC3's pins are regrouped into four labelled element groups and now carry the two **revert-detection locks** for exactly this Major (restoring the three-equivalent-identifiers list; deleting the coverage clause), so a later "simplification" back to the v1 reading turns AC3 red even where AC1/AC2 byte equality would stay green.

  - task classification, stated so review rigour is calibrated rather than guessed: **verification-mechanism work, lightweight variant** — it writes a new checker (a parity harness), the class the playbook says runs long, but it is black-box, test-only, adds no parsing of a text format, and changes no shipped behaviour.   - D1–D6 settled in the spec: (1) **the common oracle** — the two consumers do not observe alike (`bin/cluster-failures.sh` surfaces a row only when it is a FAILING span, so a clean probe makes every cluster-side assertion vacuously green), therefore every probe row carries `"status":"error"` and the two frozen outcomes are `counted` (rollup `spans: 1` AND cluster `count=1`) and `skipped` (rollup exactly `(no runs found)` AND cluster exactly `(no failure clusters found)`), with the event probe deliberately a hybrid row so a wrongly-counted event is observable on both sides; (2) a **dedicated suite** `tests/is-span-row-parity/` with its own fixtures (repo convention), a shared cross-suite fixture dir rejected, plus a mechanical single-source invariant over the probe marker and the six basenames; (3) **black-box only** — no `sed`+`eval` extraction exists to fail closed, and the suite must resolve both scripts through `$REPO_ROOT` rather than `PATH` or the mutation criteria cannot go red; (4) the **six classes** of issue #80, one row per file, with the five `kind-*` fixtures identical once the `kind` field is deleted so a classification difference is attributable, and `tests/*/fixtures/with-events.jsonl` as the source of the real event-row spelling; (5) a divergence names the drifted script and the fixture; (6) CI registration (shellcheck arg list + own `run:` step) plus a `## Appended by tasks` recipe entry.
  - known boundary, declared rather than discovered: if BOTH copies receive the same patch, parity holds and the parity half cannot see it. - [x] **T-1011** Run telemetry gains event rows alongside spans — `READY_FOR_MERGE` — spec: .shell-team/specs/T-1011-telemetry-event-rows.md
  - closed: 2026-08-01, PR #81 → develop — issue #77 stays open (Parts 2/3 = T-1012)
  - source: GitHub issue #77, **Part 1 only** — "extend run telemetry with event rows". No separate issue was filed: #77 already carries all three parts and stays the tracker, and Part 1's scope is quoted verbatim into the spec's Problem section so the split is auditable against the issue rather than against this board line. Parts 2 and 3 (`bin/gen-loop-replay.sh`, `templates/loop-replay.html`, README/docs wiring) are T-1012. Base `develop` at `08ebaea`, branch `feature/77-part1-telemetry-events`, PR body carries `Closes #77` only when Part 3 lands — this PR references #77 without closing it.
  - why it exists: telemetry records one thing, a span per sub-agent call. Every transition *between* the calls — a phase hand-off, a route-back, a gate verdict, a human stop or GO, a release — leaves no row, so a run log reads back as a bag of agent invocations rather than as a sequence of what the loop did. Part 2's replay needs the transitions; no inference over span rows reconstructs "a human stopped the loop here". The row shape has to exist first.
  - task classification, stated so review rigour is calibrated rather than guessed: this **writes and extends a verification mechanism itself** (`bin/check-run.sh` is the validator; `bin/log-run.sh` is the only writer and calls the validator in a post-write self-check). Per this repository's playbook that is the long-running class, not the pure-addition class — spec-review rigour is set at the higher standard and a multi-round rework is the expected shape, not a surprise.
  - resolved for the engineer (D1): event rows go in the **same** `<loop_id>.jsonl`, and **both** raw-row consumers learn to skip them. The consumer inventory is measured, not assumed — `grep -c field_str bin/*.sh` returns exactly two files, `bin/rollup-runs.sh` (11) and `bin/cluster-failures.sh` (5); `bin/rollup-track.sh:121` consumes rollup-runs' *stdout* and `bin/retro-inputs.sh:455` only counts `.jsonl` files, so both are outside the blast radius by measurement. **Rejected, with the measurement that kills it**: a `<loop_id>.events.jsonl` sidecar — `agents/triage-orchestrator.md:33,52,76` documents invoking both consumers as `<runs>/*.jsonl`, so a `.jsonl` sidecar is swept into that glob and corrupts them exactly as if it were in the same file, while additionally costing Part 2 a two-file merge. **Also rejected**: the implicit-skip variant (omit `run_id`/`status`/`verdict` so today's consumers ignore event rows untouched) — it genuinely works today (`rollup-runs.sh:77`, `cluster-failures.sh:114`) and is rejected anyway, because replay must group by `run_id` and a skip that happens by accident of field absence is the silent-corruption class the decision exists to remove. The skip rule is **fail-safe**: `kind` absent or `span` is a span, anything else is skipped — an unknown `kind` is by definition not a span, and reporting it is the checker's job, not the reporters'. Neither consumer gains any new output (a new `events: N` line would change a git-tracked `rollup-track.sh` artifact and `consolidate-proposals.sh`'s input).
  - resolved for the engineer (D2): the discriminator is a `kind` key whose **absence means span**, so span rows stay byte-identical (17 keys, same order, no `kind`) and no existing file is invalidated. Closed enum `span|event`; `"kind":"span"` is accepted and validated as a span; any other value, `null`, or unquoted fails closed. Shape mixing is a violation **both** ways: an event row carrying any of the **13 span-only keys**, or a span row carrying `event`. The reverse check is on `event` alone — it is the discriminator's partner key and can mean nothing else, whereas `from`/`to`/`label` are generic enough for a future span-side extension and fall under the tolerated-unknown-key rule. All new event-side key detection is **object-boundary anchored**, reusing `bin/rollup-runs.sh:60`'s precedent; the existing span-side `REQUIRED_KEYS` detection is left byte-identical because changing it would be a span-side behavior change.
  - resolved for the engineer (D3): the vocabulary is issue #77's proposal adopted verbatim as a closed enum — `handoff|rework|gate|human|release` — and the row is exactly 9 keys in a frozen order, with `loop_id`/`run_id`/`seq`/`ts` shared with spans and `seq` a **single monotonic per-run counter across both shapes** so Part 2's replay has a total order. Per-id requiredness is frozen in a table in the spec (handoff: from+to; rework: from+to+label; gate: from+label; human: label; release: none), each `label`-required row justified by the field carrying the event's whole informational content. `from`/`to` stay free-form — an adopter's phases are not this loop's phases.
  - resolved for the engineer (D4): the checker's enforce/tolerate split is enumerated, and **seven reason strings are frozen** so every negative criterion is greppable (`invalid event '<v>' (handoff|rework|gate|human|release)`, `event must be a quoted enum value`, `missing required event key(s):` — deliberately distinct from the span side's wording — `event '<id>' requires non-null <field>`, `event row carries span-only key(s):`, `span row carries event-only key: event`, `invalid kind '<v>' (span|event)` / `kind must be a quoted enum value`). Tolerated and out of contract to flag: unknown extra keys, nullable fields absent or `null`, arbitrary `label`/`from`/`to` text, trailing whitespace, CRLF, blank lines. Structure: `REQUIRED_KEYS` stays the span array byte-identical, the event side gets its own sets, `lint_line` runs the shape-independent checks first and then branches — and the event branch never runs the span required-key/status/verdict checks, because an event row is not a defective span.
  - resolved for the engineer (D5): `--event <id> [--from X] [--to Y] [--label L]`. All **13** span-only flags are usage errors in event mode (exit 2, nothing written) rather than being left for the post-write lint to catch, mirroring D2's mixing rule 1:1; `--event` with `--span` carries the frozen message `--event and --span are mutually exclusive`; `--from`/`--to`/`--label` are usage errors in span mode; an unknown `--event` value and an empty-string required value are usage errors. Version skew (new writer × old checker → row written, exit 1, never rolled back) is **confirmed and re-affirmed rather than redesigned** — it is what the header already documents for every self-check failure, every caller wraps the call in `|| true`, and telemetry is best-effort by contract; it must be written into the header instead of left to be rediscovered.
  - resolved for the engineer (D6): only `skills/run/SKILL.md`'s Telemetry section changes, with each event id mapped to a point where a span is already emitted (`handoff` at the phase boundaries, `rework` at both route-back points, `gate` at the QA/Codex verdicts plus the fail-closed seam gates, `human` at stop/GO/interrupt using the existing `interventions-classes.md` slugs as the recommended label vocabulary, `release` at close-out), alongside the `|| true` and shared-`seq` rules. **Rejected**: per-step reminders through steps 1–7 — one instruction copied seven times is the drift surface `CLAUDE.md` warns about.
  - resolved for the engineer (D7): the shape discrimination stays a **flat single-line scan; no grammar-aware tool is adopted**. Grounds: `bin/` is pure-bash zero-dependency by contract, so `jq`/python is unavailable in an adopter's repo; and the invariant needs no grammar state — every check is a per-line key test, and `log-run.sh`'s `jesc` guarantees no bare `"` inside a value, so a boundary-anchored key token cannot occur inside a string. The residual (a hand-forged escape sequence) is declared out of scope in the Input space rather than left implicit.

The event vocabulary is added to `tests/machine-tokens/run.sh` (same class as every other token group there) and proved to bite by mutation. **Parallel telemetry surfaces dispositioned up front rather than discovered later**: `skills/goal/SKILL.md` and `skills/review-response/SKILL.md` are untouched with stated reasons and locked as a protected invariant, so "you missed a parallel surface" is answered by the frozen intent instead of costing a round.

  - **DP-b modifies the tech-lead's recommendation, on the authority of the canonical issue text.** The recommendation was "a `Superseded-by` target must share the superseded entry's `Scope`". #23's stated reason for one file is that splitting "would make a local lesson that generalises unable to name its universal replacement — an un-retirable class" — i.e. `maintainer → loop` supersession is a design requirement, and a symmetric rule would forbid it. The rule adopted is **directional**: only `loop` superseded by `maintainer` is rejected (the graph stays healthy while a shipped rule vanishes with nothing replacing it in the shipped set); `loop→loop`, `maintainer→maintainer` and `maintainer→loop` stay legal. ## Format

```markdown
- [ ] **T-XXX** <one-line title> — `<STATUS_FLAG>` — spec: <specs-dir>/<slug>.md
  - <optional latest note from whichever agent touched it last>
```

`<specs-dir>` is `.shell-team/specs/` by default (or `docs/specs/` in a legacy
`tasks/` layout). The hand-off linter accepts any spec path ending in `.md`.
